Khotyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivtsi Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This cemetery, presumed established in the early 19th century, already existed by the 1820s and remained active well after WWII — its latest gravestone dates to as recently as 2016. Khotyn may have had a Karaite community as early as the 14th or 15th century, and in 1756, Jacob Frank — founder of the heterodox messianic movement later known as Frankism — found shelter here with his followers. The Jewish population peaked at 9,291 (50 percent of the town) by 1897, and the community maintained the largest library of Yiddish and Hebrew books in all of Bessarabia during the interwar period. In July 1940, under Soviet rule, much of the community was exiled to Siberia; after Romanian occupation began in July 1941, 2,000 Jews were executed within days, and 12,000 more were exiled to the Secureni camp that same month — only 300 survived.
